subject: whiplash squid
title: 4,000 Metres Down, a Squid Buried Its Head in the Mud

scenes.text: A deep sea camera filmed two white stalks. Then the stalks moved.
Four thousand metres down in the Pacific, they looked like sponges.
They weren't. They were the tentacles of a squid, buried head first in the mud.
Its body hung upside down and rigid, with just two arms sticking out.
No squid had ever been seen burying itself, let alone upside down.
Scientists think it's a disguise. In the deep sea, even a sponge might be hungry.

description:
During the SMARTEX expedition to the Clarion-Clipperton Zone, a remotely operated vehicle filmed an unknown whiplash squid about 4,000 metres down with its head buried in sediment and two long white tentacles sticking up like a sponge stalk.
It is the first squid ever recorded burying itself, and no cephalopod had been seen in that upside-down rigid pose. It may be hiding from predators or ambushing small crustaceans. The report was published in Ecology.
What else do you think is hiding down there?
first_comment: It was only the second squid spotted in that area in over 40 years of research. Would you have noticed it?
